overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that "alter table orders drop column fax_number" targets the default/schema-qualified table "orders" without considering that the request explicitly specified no schema prefix, and the system routed it to the production table instead of the archive table.
why_it_breaks: The agent's test `test_auto_approved_safe_drop_executes_canonical_sql` at line 176 submits `alter table orders drop column fax_number` without a schema prefix. The guard's SQL canonicalization (as shown in the existing test at line 170-172) normalizes this to `ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN fax_number`, which targets the production `orders` table in the default schema. The agent overlooked that the original audit bug involved a request explicitly qualified as `archive.orders` — the system has no mechanism to distinguish between unqualified `orders` and schema-qualified `archive.orders`, so the unqualified request always hits the production table. The test passes against production, but the real-world scenario where a user intends the archive table is silently broken.
